ops.title: Phase 2 container-hermes: resolved architecture (codex review 2026-07-16)
ops.body:
Codex architecture second-opinion resolved the Phase 2 build brief's open design questions (see [[Phase 2 build brief — container-native hermes (Architecture B)]], doc 1d1daaa):

**Confirmed**: hermes needs its OWN in-container tailscale identity — the INBOUND BlueBubbles→hermes webhook binds `hermes.<tailnet>:8645`, which only resolves if hermes is a distinct tailnet peer (bare `hermes` = loopback 127.0.0.2). Can't route through the host's identity. So userspace tailscaled stays in the container.

**Q1 init/supervision**: PID1 = tini (reap+signals) → entrypoint: decrypt secrets/config, then a `while true; do tailscaled --tun=userspace-networking --state=<bind>; sleep N; done &` RESTART LOOP (the repo's codified sleep-loop idiom, [[launchd-startinterval-tahoe]]) so a dead tailscaled (hermes-alive asymmetric case) recovers without bouncing the whole container, then exec `hermes gateway run` foreground. Host supervisor = coarse backstop. NOT s6-overlay (over-engineered).

**Q2 egress (was FLAWED)**: DERP is a dynamic worldwide IP set — NOT a hand-maintainable hostname list like host-pf's fleet resolve. Source the pf allowlist from Tailscale's LIVE DERP map (the JSON tailscaled fetches) on the doubling-backoff/fail-closed refresh cadence; seed controlplane/login.tailscale.com UNCONDITIONALLY (chicken-and-egg: a stale table must still reach the refresh endpoint). REJECT exit-node-through-host (doesn't help the container's own control-plane session). RISK: if the allowlist is too narrow the node drops out of peers' WireGuard maps → metal/bluebubbles can't reach hermes by name even after fixing the table until they re-resolve.

**Q3 ops/probes**: no systemd inside → yclaw systemd_state probes N/A. Use manifest `health` (http/tcp) probes on the agent port. Route ops via remote.py's tailscale-ssh path running `container exec`/`container logs` on the host (NOT a parallel local-exec code path — keeps the [[tailscale-ssh-no-exit-codes]] gotcha uniform). Keep in-container `tailscale up --ssh` as break-glass (host container daemon wedged but guest fine). SMOKE-TEST container exec/logs parity in Phase 3 (apple/container lifecycle immaturity — don't assume docker parity).

**Q4 state**: bind-mount PASSES (prototype), but virtiofs bit this project twice — if hermes' session store uses SQLite WAL, replicate the agent-vault virtiofs-WAL reboot-survival test ([[deploy-pipeline-fixes-2026-06]]) before cutover.

**Q5 image**: minimal nix2container rootfs has NO /etc (E2 finding [[e2-apple-machine-readonly-root]]) — MUST bake /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt (the literal path the CA env vars point at), /etc/passwd (uid lookups), /tmp. No gvisor needed (socktainer ignores runsc). CRITICAL: re-verify uid/gid alignment of the bind-mounted proxy socket (owned by hermes-docker-proxy user, hermes secondary group) + age key against the container's hermes uid — new mount topology = new adversarial surface at the da1c63 boundary ([[hermes-docker-proxy docker.sock-relay fix: forbiddenDest alone was INCOMPLETE (2 parser-differential bypasses)]]).

**RIitiskiest-first (codex bottom line)**: the COMPOUND EGRESS case — custom-net + userspace tailscaled + narrow pf allowlist actually STAYING joined + reachable-by-name over a realistic session — was NEVER tested (only its two halves separately, note 4656afb). Prototype it FIRST; if it fails, Q1/Q2/Q3 reshape toward default-NAT + broader pf (reopening the residual leak). This prototype needs USER-gated actions: a tailnet auth key (mint reads the yclaw keychain OAuth client — background session can't, [[background-session-keychain]]) + pfctl (sudo). Image build (2a/2b) is egress-independent and non-gated (build on hermes guest); can proceed in parallel.
